display.purpose: The one H1 of every page.

subhead.purpose: A heading inside a plate or on the key page, and the second level of rendered Markdown.

title.purpose: H3s: questions, per-system checks, changelog groups.

answer.purpose: The sentence under an H1 that answers it, in Second Ink.

lead.purpose: The paragraph that answers a section heading, in Navy Ink.

body.purpose: Reading text at the 52ch measure (66 to 72 characters).

table.purpose: Cells of a table of figures and every row head, on tabular figures.

table-head.purpose: Column heads, in Second Ink and normal case.

caption.purpose: What a figure shows, set in italic in Second Ink.

plate-title.purpose: A plate's name at its head and the curve's notes, set in italic in Second Ink.

label.purpose: Button labels; navigation links at weight 600.

code.purpose: Code, commands, file names and network addresses, with ligatures off.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: The site's one authored motion: the home page's tide curve draws itself once on load, from a visible state. Reduced motion shows the finished drawing.

motion.name: colour-change
motion.purpose: Hover colour changes on buttons, the primary fill darkening and the secondary tint.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition duration is zero, so nothing moves.

narrative.overview:
The site reads every plan limit the way an almanac reads the tide: as a predicted time. When a window resets, and when it would run out at the pace it is going, are set in tables of tabular figures and on curves that climb towards a dashed high-water line at 100%. The look is the nautical chart's own. Flat fields of chart blue, fine vector line work and navy ink carry everything, and one chart magenta is held back for the action and for cautions, much as a chart keeps magenta for its lights and warnings.

Each page descends as it scrolls, from chart white through the shallow and mid blue fields to the navy deep of the closing band and footer, one tone to a band. Sofia Sans carries every word in three widths: condensed for headings, actions and chart labels, regular for reading, semi-condensed with tabular figures for tables and captions. Density is moderate: tables carry real numbers, reading blocks stay short, and generous space separates the bands. The only pictures are captures of the real QuotaDial window with example accounts. Light and dark follow the visitor's system as the day chart and the night chart, and every colour token has its night pair.

The system rejects the usage-tracker category's centred app hero with a floating popover, the dark documentation template with icon cards, the cream almanac with a serif display and hairlines, and nautical ornament of every kind.
keyCharacteristics: Predicted times in tables and curves, read against a dashed high-water line at 100%.
Depth bands that descend each page from chart white to the navy deep.
One reserved accent, chart magenta, in four places and nowhere else.
Sofia Sans in three widths for every word; JetBrains Mono only for code, commands, file names and addresses.
Flat fields and hairline line work: no shadows, and a 2 px corner on every box.
Plates framed with a neatline and a graduated scale, in place of cards.

rules.name: The Four Places Rule
rules.body: Magenta appears in exactly four places: the primary action's fill, a runs-out-first prediction, the focus ring and the unsigned-build caution. Never on a heading, a name, a link in running text or decoration, and never as text on the Row Band over Mid Field, where it falls to 4.47:1.

rules.name: The Words First Rule
rules.body: Magenta never carries a meaning alone. A runs-out-first cell says "Runs out Tue 18:40" in words, and the curve's magenta prediction ends in its label.

rules.name: The Line Blue Rule
rules.body: Line blue draws and never writes.

rules.name: The Three Widths Rule
rules.body: Condensed speaks, regular reads, semi-condensed counts. Headings, actions, labels and chart notes are condensed; paragraphs and the sentences in a table of words are regular; figures, times, table heads, row heads and captions are semi-condensed. A width never takes another width's job.

rules.name: The True Italic Rule
rules.body: A width that slopes loads its own italic file beside its upright, from the same package. The browser never invents a slope.

rules.name: The Unbroken Time Rule
rules.body: A time, a duration or a file name in a table never breaks across two lines ("Tue 18:40", "1 d 15 h", "QuotaDial_<version>_universal.dmg"). When a column cannot hold them whole, the layout changes and the time does not: on a phone the home table sets each row as two lines, and the files table stacks each file under its system. In running text a long file name may break only after an underscore or a hyphen.

rules.name: The Reading Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text holds 66 to 72 characters a line: the measure token, 52ch (`--container-measure`). A ch is the width of a zero, wider than Sofia Sans' average letter, which is why 52ch gives 66 to 72 characters.

rules.name: The Descent Rule
rules.body: Bands descend: chart white first, then shallow, then mid, then the deep for the close and the footer. One tone to a band, and no page climbs back towards white.

rules.name: The Unequal Columns Rule
rules.body: Things that come in threes sit in columns of unequal width (5:4:6 on the home page, 4:3:5 on the download page), never in three equal cards.

rules.name: The Changing Family Rule
rules.body: Down the home page no two sections in a row share a layout family; a new long page keeps the same habit, so it never reads as a template.

rules.name: The Flat Chart Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from field tone and line work, never from shadow. A surface that needs to stand forward takes a different field or a neatline.

rules.name: The Two Pixel Rule
rules.body: Every box (a button, a plate, a code block, a notice) takes a 2 px corner. No pills and no soft rounded cards; the only round forms are the curve's prediction dot and the mark.

rules.name: The Neatline Rule
rules.body: Every plate is framed as a chart plate is: a hairline neatline 8 px in, with a graduated scale in the margin, drawn as line work and never as texture or a bevel.

dos: Do keep magenta to its four places: the primary fill, a runs-out-first prediction, the focus ring and the unsigned-build caution.
Do band table rows by what they belong to (a provider, a system, an account), alternating the Row Band tint group by group.
Do align words left and figures and times right in every table, on tabular figures.
Do frame every plate with its neatline and graduated scale, and name a titled plate at its head in condensed italic.
Do descend the bands down the page: chart white, shallow, mid, then the deep for the close and the footer.
Do say every caution in words as well as in magenta.
Do keep a time on one line, and change the layout when a column cannot hold it.
Do keep reading text at the reading measure, 52ch (66 to 72 characters).
Do show the app only as a real capture matched to the theme, captioned as example accounts.
Do keep motion to one authored moment, the home curve drawing once in 900 ms, with reduced motion showing the end state.
donts: Don't stripe rows by position or rule a line under every row.
Don't set a label, a kicker or a plate title above a heading; a heading carries itself.
Don't use magenta on a heading, a name, a link in running text or decoration.
Don't set Line Blue as text.
Don't cast a shadow, blur a surface or use glass.
Don't round a box past 2 px: no pill buttons and no soft cards.
Don't use a cream, parchment or warm paper ground; the ground is a cool chart white.
Don't draw nautical ornament (anchors, rope, ship's wheels, waves as decoration); a curve on this site always plots real numbers.
Don't centre the first screen, or lay content out as three equal cards or icon-in-a-square grids.
Don't use gradient text, neon on black, or monospace outside code, commands, file names and addresses.
Don't draw an interface out of boxes to look like the app.
Don't reveal sections on scroll or add a second moving moment.
Don't fold answers into an accordion.
Don't recolour or redraw the mark.
